decisions.reason: The peak-alignment decision concerns only the Hero V and É accent. The separate second-V reach issue is already represented as execution evidence and does not change its established requirement values.
The approved Hero V remains the fixed reference geometry; exact peak alignment can be achieved by positioning the É accent relative to it and does not necessarily modify the Hero V geometry.
The shared terminal gesture remains unchanged. The new requirement is a positional peak-alignment constraint specifically owned by the Hero-derived É accent requirement.
The Hero V–accent peak alignment does not alter the E and L construction rules. Their separate same-message redesign is already represented by an existing MODIFY.
Exact geometric alignment of the Hero V and É accent does not change the broader brand-expression values.
The source decision changes geometric positioning, not the deferred champagne-gold material treatment or its design role.
The source establishes a specific Hero V–accent derivation constraint without changing the existing composition, kerning, rhythm, hierarchy, or case-treatment rules.
Peak alignment does not affect the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram.
